learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic definitions and principles of supramolecular chemistry, widely used for the construction of novel materials.
Correlate nanostructure architecture with the chemical structure of its components.
Identify non-covalent interactions employed in self-organization and use this knowledge to understand and design new molecules and nanostructures.
Work in multidisciplinary environments requiring basic supramolecular chemistry understanding (within the framework of a diploma thesis or Erasmus).

syllabus_topics: Supramolecular Chemistry: Definition and basic principles
Self-organization: Amphiphiles, polymers, helical polymers, supramolecular polymers, peptides, proteins, oligonucleotides
Presentation and analysis of research studies from current literature

assessment_methods.method: Seminar (oral presentation of a research paper from current literature)
Paper (written presentation of the research paper from current literature)

assessment_rules: Evaluation is based on a seminar (oral presentation of a research paper from current literature) weighted at 60%, a written presentation of the research paper weighted at 20%, and a final exam with short-answer questions weighted at 20%.
bibliography: Core Concepts in Supramolecular Chemistry and Nanochemistry, Jonathan W. Steed, David R. Turner and Karl J. Wallace. John Wiley & Sons, Ltd: Chichester. 2007.
Supramolecular chemistry: Concepts and perspectives, J.-M. Lehn, VCH, Weinheim 1995.
Application of supramolecular chemistry, Schneider, H.J., CRC Press 2012.
degree: Materials Science and Engineering — Πτυχίο Τμήματος Επιστήμης και Μηχανικής Υλικών (first cycle, 240 ECTS, curriculum ΕΜΥ)
